narrative.intro: Loyal Source Government Services recorded $1.8B in federal contract obligations in FY2026 to date. Loyal Source Government Services won 15 awards with an average award size of $122M. Loyal Source Government Services obligations are up 103.0% year over year. Loyal Source Government Services obligations rose through recent fiscal years: $244M in FY21, $173M in FY22, $374M in FY23, $546M in FY24, $900M in FY25, and $1.8B in FY26. Loyal Source Government Services receives the bulk of FY2026 to date obligations from the Department of Veterans Affairs, which obligated $1.8B. Loyal Source Government Services also received obligations from the Department of Homeland Security totaling $57.6M and from the Department of Defense totaling $706K. Loyal Source Government Services primary markets are health-related: Offices of Physicians (except Mental Health Specialists) at $1.8B and Temporary Help Services at $57M. Loyal Source Government Services has smaller presences in Offices of All Other Miscellaneous Health Practitioners at $1.3M and Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology) at $500. Current-year totals are partial and reported fiscal year to date.

sections.heading: How have Loyal Source Government Services obligations trended over the last five fiscal years?
sections.body: Loyal Source Government Services obligations increased from $244M in FY21 to $173M in FY22, $374M in FY23, $546M in FY24, $900M in FY25, and $1.8B in FY26. Loyal Source Government Services year-over-year change is up 103.0% in the current fiscal-year-to-date period.

sections.heading: Who are Loyal Source Government Services top buyers and what markets do they serve?
sections.body: The Department of Veterans Affairs is the top buyer for Loyal Source Government Services with $1.8B in FY2026 to date. Loyal Source Government Services also received $57.6M from the Department of Homeland Security and $706K from the Department of Defense. Loyal Source Government Services primary markets are Offices of Physicians (except Mental Health Specialists) at $1.8B and Temporary Help Services at $57M, with smaller activity in Offices of All Other Miscellaneous Health Practitioners at $1.3M and Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology) at $500.

faq.a: Loyal Source Government Services has federal contract obligations of $1.8B in FY2026 to date. Loyal Source Government Services won 15 awards in the period and the average award size is $122M. Loyal Source Government Services obligations are up 103.0% year over year.

faq.q: Which agencies buy from Loyal Source Government Services?
faq.a: The Department of Veterans Affairs is the largest buyer of Loyal Source Government Services with $1.8B in FY2026 to date. Loyal Source Government Services also received $57.6M from the Department of Homeland Security and $706K from the Department of Defense.

faq.q: What does Loyal Source Government Services sell to the government?
faq.a: Loyal Source Government Services sells primarily physician and health-related services, led by Offices of Physicians (except Mental Health Specialists) at $1.8B and Temporary Help Services at $57M. Loyal Source Government Services also has obligations in Offices of All Other Miscellaneous Health Practitioners at $1.3M and in Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology) at $500.
